Find examples with likely label errors

Source: R/issues.R
find_label_issues.Rd

Flags examples whose given label is likely wrong, using one of the rank and prune rules of confident learning (Northcutt et al., 2021, Sec. 3.2). Every rule needs out-of-sample predicted probabilities, for example from cross-validation.

  • "prune_by_noise_rate" (default): for every pair of given label i and true label j, the estimated number of examples in that cell of the joint (see estimate_joint()) is flagged among the examples labelled i, choosing those where p[j] - p[i] is largest.

  • "prune_by_class": for every given label i, the estimated number of mislabelled examples is flagged among the examples labelled i, choosing those with the lowest self-confidence p[i].

  • "both": examples flagged by both rules above.

  • "confident_learning": examples in the off-diagonal cells of the confident joint (see confident_joint()).

  • "predicted_neq_given": examples whose most likely class differs from the given label. A simple baseline that ignores class imbalance.

As in the cleanlab Python package, an example whose most likely class is its given label is never flagged, whichever rule is used: the classifier then offers no evidence against the label.

Flagged examples are candidates for review, not proven errors: ambiguous examples that genuinely fit several classes are flagged too.

Usage

find_label_issues(
  x,
  ...,
  filter_by = c("prune_by_noise_rate", "prune_by_class", "both", "confident_learning",
    "predicted_neq_given"),
  rank_by = c("self_confidence", "normalized_margin", "confidence_weighted_entropy"),
  frac_noise = 1,
  min_examples_per_class = 1
)

Arguments

x

Labels or an object holding labels and predicted probabilities. See Description.

...

Passed to label_inputs(): for example pred_probs when x is a label vector, or truth when x is a data frame.

filter_by

Rule used to flag examples, see Description.

rank_by

Label quality score reported in label_quality, see label_quality_scores(). Sort by it to review the most suspicious examples first.

frac_noise

Fraction of the estimated number of label errors to flag, between 0 and 1. Only used by the "prune_by_*" and "both" rules. Lower values flag fewer, more certain examples.

min_examples_per_class

The rules never flag so many examples of a given label that fewer than this number would remain unflagged.

Value

A tibble with one row per example, in the order of the input, and columns

  • .row: the row identifier (the .row of resampled predictions, or the position in the input);

  • given: the given label;

  • predicted: the class with the largest predicted probability;

  • label_quality: the label quality score chosen by rank_by;

  • is_label_issue: whether the example is flagged.

References

Northcutt, C., Jiang, L., & Chuang, I. (2021). Confident learning: Estimating uncertainty in dataset labels. Journal of Artificial Intelligence Research, 70, 1373–1411. doi:10.1613/jair.1.12125

See also

health_summary() for a class-level overview.

Examples

sim <- simulate_label_noise(n = 500, noise_rate = 0.1, seed = 1)
issues <- find_label_issues(sim, truth = given)
issues
#> # A tibble: 500 × 5
#>     .row given predicted label_quality is_label_issue
#>    <int> <fct> <fct>             <dbl> <lgl>         
#>  1     1 A     A                 0.722 FALSE         
#>  2     2 A     C                 0.188 FALSE         
#>  3     3 B     B                 0.432 FALSE         
#>  4     4 D     D                 0.690 FALSE         
#>  5     5 A     C                 0.223 TRUE          
#>  6     6 C     C                 0.516 FALSE         
#>  7     7 D     D                 0.483 FALSE         
#>  8     8 B     B                 0.834 FALSE         
#>  9     9 B     B                 0.637 FALSE         
#> 10    10 A     A                 0.484 FALSE         
#> # ℹ 490 more rows

# Review the most suspicious examples first
flagged <- issues[issues$is_label_issue, ]
head(flagged[order(flagged$label_quality), ])
#> # A tibble: 6 × 5
#>    .row given predicted label_quality is_label_issue
#>   <int> <fct> <fct>             <dbl> <lgl>         
#> 1   424 B     A               0.00428 TRUE          
#> 2   234 A     D               0.00632 TRUE          
#> 3   370 C     B               0.00650 TRUE          
#> 4   392 B     A               0.00956 TRUE          
#> 5   376 C     B               0.0105  TRUE          
#> 6    53 A     B               0.0121  TRUE          

# How well did it do on this simulation?
table(flagged = issues$is_label_issue, mislabelled = sim$given != sim$true)
#>        mislabelled
#> flagged FALSE TRUE
#>   FALSE   408   11
#>   TRUE     34   47
